title: Combiner les négations et exprimer une restriction
summary: Express not anymore, never anything and precise restrictions; recognize spoken ne omission.
objectives: Combine compatible negative expressions without an extra pas.
Place que next to what is restricted in a compound tense.
Restore ne in an informal negative sentence.

sources.label: B1 public topic index (coverage reference only)

sections.title: Two negative meanings can work together
paragraphs: French can combine negative expressions to deny different parts of one situation. Ne ... plus rien means not anything anymore; ne ... plus jamais means never again; ne ... jamais personne means never anybody. These do not automatically cancel into a positive statement.

With a compound tense, plus, jamais and object rien normally come before the participle, while object personne and nulle part normally follow it. Use one ne before the finite verb or auxiliary. Do not add pas to the combinations taught here. This is not permission to stack any negative words randomly: each must contribute a clear meaning.
points: Vocabulary: un abonnement (masculine), a subscription; une notification (feminine), a notification.
Plus in a negative sentence means no longer; positive plus can mean more, so context and pronunciation matter.

examples.french: Je **ne reçois plus rien** depuis lundi.
examples.english: I haven't been receiving anything since Monday.
examples.note: No longer plus nothing: an ongoing absence.

examples.french: Nous **n'avons jamais vu personne** dans ce bureau.
examples.english: We have never seen anybody in this office.
examples.note: Jamais precedes vu, personne follows it.

examples.french: Elle **ne travaillera plus jamais** le dimanche.
examples.english: She will never work on Sundays again.
examples.note: Plus jamais combines no longer and ever.
A negative subject combines with a negative object.

mistakes.avoid: Je ne reçois pas plus rien.
mistakes.why: To mean I no longer receive anything, plus rien supplies the negative meaning; do not add pas.

sections.title: Ne ... que restricts; it does not deny
paragraphs: Ne ... que means only. It does not mean not. In a compound tense, ne goes before the auxiliary, but que goes immediately before the restricted part: Je n'ai lu que l'introduction restricts what I read; Je n'ai lu le rapport que lundi restricts when.

Keep the article required by the positive meaning: Je n'ai acheté que des fruits, I bought only fruit. This differs from Je n'ai pas acheté de fruits, I did not buy fruit. For restricting the subject itself, seul or seulement is often clearer: Seule Lina a répondu, only Lina answered.
points: Que becomes qu' before a vowel.
Ne ... pas que means not only and is a different meaning from ne ... que.

examples.note: The number of messages is restricted.

examples.english: I sent the messages only yesterday.

examples.note: Des remains because this is a restriction, not an ordinary negative denial.

examples.french: Elle **n'a pas lu que** le résumé.
examples.english: She did not read only the summary.
examples.note: Pas que denies the restriction: she read more than the summary.

mistakes.avoid: Je n'ai que lu deux pages.
mistakes.prefer: Je n'ai lu que deux pages.
mistakes.why: To restrict the number of pages, put que directly before deux pages. The other placement would focus on the action and does not express the intended restriction naturally.

sections.title: Recognize informal negatives without copying them everywhere
paragraphs: In spontaneous conversation, speakers often omit ne/n'. The remaining pas, plus, jamais, rien or personne carries the negative information: J'ai rien reçu. Keep ne in careful writing and in these controlled written exercises unless the prompt explicitly requests the informal version.

Do not simply remove all negative words. J'ai reçu is affirmative. With plus, omission can increase ambiguity between more and no longer; context becomes important. Ne omission is a register feature, not proof that a speaker does not understand grammar.
points: Restore n' before a vowel: J'ai pas becomes Je n'ai pas.
Subject negatives can omit ne orally too: Personne sait becomes Personne ne sait in careful writing.

examples.french:
Oral: J'ai **rien** reçu.
Careful writing: Je **n'ai rien** reçu.
examples.english:
Spoken: I haven't received anything.
Careful writing: I haven't received anything.
examples.note: The meaning is preserved; the register changes.

examples.french:
Oral: Elle vient **plus**.
Careful writing: Elle **ne** vient **plus**.
examples.english:
Spoken: She doesn't come anymore.
Careful writing: She doesn't come anymore.
examples.note: Here plus has its negative no-longer meaning.

sections.title: Limiter une action et reconnaître un ordre possible
paragraphs: When only limits what someone did rather than which object they handled, que can precede the past participle: il n'a que déplacé le meuble focuses on moving it, not repairing or cleaning it. To make that action focus especially clear, use ne faire que + infinitive: il n'a fait que déplacer le meuble. By contrast, il n'a déplacé que le meuble restricts the object moved. Work backward from the intended contrast before choosing the position of que.

Never again has two accepted orders: plus jamais and jamais plus. The first is the ordinary default used earlier; the second is also standard. Do not extend that flexibility to every combination: plus rien and plus personne keep plus first in the ordinary meanings nothing anymore and nobody anymore. One written ne frames the relevant verb group.
points: Vocabulary: un meuble (masculine), a piece of furniture. Restriction affirms a limited action; it is not equivalent to denying that action.

examples.french: Il **n'a fait que déplacer** le meuble ; il ne l'a pas réparé.
examples.english: He only moved the piece of furniture; he did not repair it.

examples.french: Il **n'a déplacé que le meuble** ; les cartons sont restés en place.
examples.english: He moved only the piece of furniture; the boxes stayed where they were.

examples.french: Nous ne signerons **jamais plus / plus jamais** sans lire.
examples.english: We will never again sign without reading.

practice.prompt: Supply the two words meaning nothing anymore: Je ne comprends ___.
practice.explanation: Plus rien combines cessation with no object.

practice.prompt: Supply the two words meaning never again: Nous ne recommencerons ___.
practice.explanation: Plus jamais and jamais plus both express never again.

practice.prompt: Supply que or qu': Elle n'a réservé ___ une chambre.
Restore the missing written negation in this exact sentence: J'ai pas compris.
practice.explanation: Restore ne, elided as n' before ai.

practice.prompt: Rewrite using ne ... que to restrict the object: J'ai acheté seulement un billet.
practice.explanation: Que goes before un billet, not before acheté.

practice.prompt: Rewrite with ne ... que to restrict the day: Nous avons répondu seulement mardi.
practice.explanation: Que directly precedes the restricted time mardi.

practice.prompt: Arrange only these three words to complete the sentence: jamais / personne / rencontré. Elle n'a ___ ici.
practice.explanation: Jamais precedes the participle; personne follows it.

practice.prompt: Supply the missing written negator: Personne ___ lui a rien expliqué.
practice.explanation: Ne goes before the object pronoun and auxiliary group.

practice.prompt: Restore ne in the exact informal sentence: Elle travaille plus. The intended meaning is she no longer works.
practice.explanation: Restoring ne makes the intended negative reading explicit.

practice.prompt: Choose the article for the restriction meaning we bought only flowers: Nous n'avons acheté que ___ fleurs.
practice.explanation: Ne ... que is restrictive; it does not trigger the ordinary negative de.

practice.prompt: Which sentence means she read more than just the title?
choices: Elle n'a lu que le titre.
Elle n'a pas lu que le titre.
answers: Elle n'a pas lu que le titre.

practice.prompt: Arrange only plus / rien / reçu: Je n'ai ___ depuis jeudi.
practice.explanation: Both plus and rien precede the participle reçu.

practice.prompt: Restore the missing ne in: Personne sait pourquoi.
practice.explanation: Keep the negative subject and restore ne before sait.

practice.prompt: Rewrite with ne ... que, restricting the amount: Elle a travaillé seulement deux heures.
answers: Elle n'a travaillé que deux heures.
practice.explanation: Que restricts the duration, not the verb.

practice.prompt: Remove the single unnecessary word to mean we will never return there again: Nous n'y retournerons pas plus jamais.
practice.explanation: Plus jamais supplies the intended negative meaning.

practice.prompt: Supply que or qu' in the time restriction: Je ne l'ai appris ___ aujourd'hui.
practice.explanation: Que elides before aujourd'hui and restricts when the information was learned.

practice.prompt: The technician looked at the machine but did not test or repair it. Choose the restriction that focuses on the action, not on which object was inspected.
choices: Il n'a fait que regarder la machine.
Il n'a regardé que la machine.
answers: Il n'a fait que regarder la machine.
practice.explanation: Ne faire que + infinitive restricts the action; que la machine would instead exclude other things looked at.

practice.prompt: Use ne ... que around faire in the passé composé to restrict the action: Elle ___ recopier le texte. Supply only the missing verb group.
practice.explanation: Elle n'a fait que recopier means copying was all she did; the following verb remains infinitive.

practice.prompt: Complete with two words meaning never again, beginning with jamais: Je ne voyagerai ___ sans assurance.
practice.explanation: Jamais plus is standard as well as plus jamais. The prompt fixes the starting word, not a difference in meaning.

production_task.prompt: Explain a notification problem to customer support in careful written French. Say that you no longer receive anything, identify the only message received before that period, and state that nobody has explained anything.
production_task.model_answer: Je ne reçois plus rien depuis mercredi. Je n'ai reçu qu'un message automatique mardi. Personne ne m'a rien expliqué. Je voudrais savoir si mon abonnement est toujours actif.
production_task.translation: I haven't been receiving anything since Wednesday. I received only one automated message on Tuesday. Nobody has explained anything to me. I would like to know whether my subscription is still active.
rubric: Use compatible negative combinations in the right order.
Put que directly before the restricted object.
Keep ne in the customer-service message.
Distinguish receiving only one message from receiving none.
